subject: Request: temporary SLA relief for beta model during Bluebridge pilot ramp
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Lydia Wong <ldwong@bluebridge.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary SLA relief for beta model during Bluebridge pilot ramp

Lydia / Bluebridge team —

Thanks again for agreeing to run the pilot with our new gen-embedder-preview model. As discussed during yesterday's call, the model is still in a preview stage and we expect periodic latency spikes during warm-up and KV cache population for the first 4–6 weeks.

To make progress on the integration we would like to request a timeboxed SLA adjustment for the pilot window rather than the full production SLOs in your contract. Proposal summary:

- Duration: 6 weeks from pilot start (with a checkpoint at week 2 and week 4)
- Latency: allow 99th percentile latency up to 2.5s for customer-facing search for the duration; maintain 95th percentile below 600ms where possible
- Uptime: standard uptime target stays in place; we will provide fallbacks to a cached older model if throughput/latency degrades beyond the tolerance window
- Mitigations: continuous telemetry dashboard (token-level latency), automatic model fallback, and a dedicated on-call rotation for the pilot
- Credits: we are prepared to grant a pro-rated usage credit if incidents materially impact your launch milestones

Attachments: bluebridge_pilot_mop.pdf (operational plan), proposed_sla_patch.docx (redlined addendum).

Marissa / Jordan / Hannah — I need help quantifying the exact SLO text we should ask procurement to accept and any legal guardrails we should propose (timebox language, rollback triggers, financial remediation caps).

Lydia — please confirm that the proposed temporary 99th percentile bound and timebox sound acceptable; if you have more precise latency targets for specific patient flows, share them and we’ll incorporate into the pilot MoP.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lydia Wong <ldwong@bluebridge.health>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA relief for beta model during Bluebridge pilot ramp

Priyom —

Thanks for the clear ask. A few legal/commercial points to start with:

- Timebox: recommend 6 weeks with an optional 2-week extension only if both parties sign off on milestone progress.
- Rollback trigger: define a customer-impact threshold (e.g., 3 incident windows > 5 minutes in a 7-day span) that automatically reverts to the standard model fallback and reinstates regular SLOs.
- Financial cap: limit remediation to a single pro-rated usage credit equal to the pilot committed spend (we can negotiate higher in enterprise SKUs).
- Contract language: we should avoid broad "SLA waiver" phrasing; instead, include an "Operational Pilot Addendum" that enumerates exact metric deltas, mitigation steps, and the review cadence. I'm attaching some standard language snippets in proposed_sla_patch.docx.

Jordan — can you quantify expected KV-cache warm-up time and any short-term throughput degradation we should disclose to the customer? I want an internal note to cite in the addendum (examples like "expected 12–48 hour warm-up for new shards; highest variance during initial 100K requests").

Lydia — if you can get procurement to accept an addendum phrased as "Operational Pilot Addendum" rather than an SLA permanent change, it will be easier to process. Also please send any latency targets by flow (search, record retrieval, autocomplete) so we can map thresholds.

—Marissa
Senior Sales Counsel
Redwood Inference

From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>, Lydia Wong <ldwong@bluebridge.health>
Date: Fri, 05 Jun 2026 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA relief for beta model during Bluebridge pilot ramp

Marissa / team —

Quick technical note to quantify warm-up behavior:

- Warm-up: first steady-state warm-up for a new tenant typically takes ~6–24 hours for small traffic, but for the volume you're planning (estimate ~200 rps peak) expect 24–72 hours for KV and prefill mechanisms to stabilize.
- Spikes: we sometimes see 95th→99th percentile widening when a cold host needs to pull large KV segments or during background quantization. That can drive short 1–3s spikes for isolated requests early in the ramp.
- Mitigations we will run: aggressive prefix caching for common patient queries, pre-warming during off-hours, and an autoscale buffer to add nodes during the first 72 hours of heavy ramp.

I recommend we propose a rolling ramp with a max initial concurrency cap (e.g., 50 rps) for 48 hours, then increase in steps to full traffic to avoid broad exposure. That also gives us deterministic checkpoints for the addendum.

—Jordan
Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Lydia Wong <ldwong@bluebridge.health>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bluebridge Health Procurement <procurement@bluebridge.health>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 08 Jun 2026 08:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA relief for beta model during Bluebridge pilot ramp

Priyom / team —

Thanks for the details and the proposed mitigations. We discussed internally with product and procurement. High-level response:

- We can accept a timeboxed Operational Pilot Addendum. Our primary constraint is patient-facing search latency: we need 95th percentile at or below 600ms for critical flows (search results that feed the clinician UI).
- For the pilot only, Bluebridge can accept 99th percentile up to 2.5s for non-critical background/analytics flows and up to 1.8s for patient-facing flows, provided the first two weeks include daily check-ins and an automated rollback if we hit more than 2 "major incidents" in a rolling 7-day window.
- Procurement asks that the addendum include: exact metric names (p95_search_latency_ms, p99_search_latency_ms), the timebox, a single remediation credit cap, and a defined sign-off flow at week 2 or earlier.

I've attached a spreadsheet with per-flow latency targets (bbh_latency_requirements.xlsx) and a draft language piece we can send to procurement. If you can provide a draft Operational Pilot Addendum by EOD Tuesday, we'll try to have procurement review it the same day.

Best,
Lydia Wong
Director, Product Operations
Bluebridge Health

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Bluebridge Health Procurement <procurement@bluebridge.health>, Lydia Wong <ldwong@bluebridge.health>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 09 Jun 2026 15:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary SLA relief for beta model during Bluebridge pilot ramp

Lydia / Procurement —

Appreciate the quick alignment. We will produce a draft Operational Pilot Addendum that:

- Names the exact metrics (p95_search_latency_ms, p99_search_latency_ms),
- Specifies the 6-week timebox with a 2-week review and an opt-in 2-week extension,
- Includes rollback triggers (>=2 major incidents in 7 days) and a single pro-rated remediation credit cap,
- Documents the ramp plan (48h 50 rps -> 72h 150 rps -> full load) and mitigation steps (prefill, pre-warm, autoscale buffer).

Action items: Jordan will provide a short technical appendix with expected warm-up windows; Marissa will craft the addendum language and send a redline. I aim to circulate the draft addendum and a DocuSign-ready attachment by EOD Tuesday so procurement can loop in legal.

Hannah — can your ops team stand by for the first-week daily check-ins? Also include the Grafana link and on-call rotation in the addendum.

I'll follow up with the draft and the hubspot deal update.

Thanks —
Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
